pairs.description: Tenofovir is eliminated by glomerular filtration and active tubular secretion and is itself associated with renal tubular injury; NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandin-mediated perfusion and are nephrotoxic at high or repeated doses.
pairs.clinical_significance: Acute renal failure has been reported after initiation of high-dose or multiple NSAIDs in HIV-infected patients with risk factors for renal dysfunction who appeared stable on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate.
pairs.recommendation: Tenofovir DF is avoided with concurrent or recent high-dose or multiple NSAID use; alternatives to NSAIDs (e.g., paracetamol) are considered in patients at risk for renal dysfunction. If coadministered, serum creatinine, creatinine clearance, urine glucose and urine protein are monitored.
pairs.source_attribution: VIREAD (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5.2 and 7.1

pairs.description: Mefenamic acid is an NSAID; NSAID-induced reduction in renal perfusion adds to the tubular nephrotoxicity risk of tenofovir, which is renally eliminated.
pairs.clinical_significance: The tenofovir DF label warns of acute renal failure after initiation of high-dose or multiple NSAIDs in patients with renal risk factors, and lists NSAIDs among drugs that may increase tenofovir concentrations.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid concurrent or recent high-dose or multiple NSAID use with tenofovir DF; prefer a non-NSAID analgesic in patients at renal risk, and monitor renal function if the combination is used.
pairs.source_attribution: VIREAD (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5.2 and 7.1 (NSAID class statement)

pairs.description: Tenofovir and aciclovir are both eliminated by the kidney partly via active tubular secretion; coadministration may increase serum concentrations of either drug.
pairs.clinical_significance: Higher tenofovir exposure increases the risk of renal adverse reactions (acute kidney injury, proximal tubulopathy/Fanconi syndrome).
pairs.recommendation: Monitor renal function (serum creatinine, creatinine clearance, urine glucose/protein, phosphorus in CKD) during coadministration, particularly with high-dose intravenous aciclovir or pre-existing renal impairment.
pairs.source_attribution: VIREAD (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7.1 Drugs Affecting Renal Function

pairs.description: The tenofovir disoproxil fumarate component of TLD is renally eliminated and nephrotoxic; NSAIDs impair renal perfusion.
pairs.clinical_significance: Labels for lamivudine/tenofovir DF combinations state that coadministration should be avoided with concurrent or recent use of a nephrotoxic agent such as high-dose or multiple NSAIDs, because of the risk of acute renal failure.
pairs.recommendation: Prefer paracetamol for analgesia in people on TLD, especially with renal risk factors; if an NSAID is needed, use briefly at the lowest dose with monitoring of renal function.
pairs.source_attribution: CIMDUO (lamivudine and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) FDA label (DailyMed), Warnings (new onset or worsening renal impairment) and Drug Interactions; applies to the TDF/3TC component of TLD

pairs.description: Mefenamic acid is an NSAID; NSAID-related renal hypoperfusion adds to the tubular nephrotoxicity risk of the tenofovir DF component of TLD.
pairs.clinical_significance: Labels for lamivudine/tenofovir DF combinations advise avoiding concurrent or recent use of nephrotoxic agents such as high-dose or multiple NSAIDs.
pairs.recommendation: Prefer a non-NSAID analgesic; if used (e.g., short courses for dysmenorrhea), keep to the lowest dose and shortest duration and monitor renal function in those with renal risk factors.
pairs.source_attribution: CIMDUO (lamivudine and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) FDA label (DailyMed), Warnings and Drug Interactions (NSAID class statement); applies to the TDF/3TC component of TLD

pairs.description: Aciclovir competes with tenofovir for active renal tubular secretion; coadministration may increase serum concentrations of tenofovir and/or aciclovir.
pairs.clinical_significance: Raised tenofovir exposure increases the risk of renal toxicity; the combination is common in people with HIV treated for herpes simplex or varicella-zoster infection.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor renal function during coadministration, especially with intravenous or high-dose aciclovir, dehydration or pre-existing renal impairment; adjust aciclovir dose to creatinine clearance.
pairs.source_attribution: CIMDUO (lamivudine and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) FDA label (DailyMed), Drug Interactions: drugs affecting renal function (acyclovir, valacyclovir)

pairs.description: Dolutegravir inhibits the renal transporters OCT2 and MATE1, reducing tubular secretion of metformin. Dolutegravir 50 mg once daily increased metformin AUC by 79% and Cmax by 66%; twice-daily dolutegravir increased AUC by 145%.
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased metformin exposure raises the risk of gastrointestinal adverse effects and, particularly with renal impairment, lactic acidosis; stopping dolutegravir can reduce glycaemic control.
pairs.recommendation: Consider metformin dose adjustment when starting or stopping dolutegravir; the US prescribing information suggests limiting total daily metformin to 1,000 mg when starting either drug. Monitor renal function and blood glucose when starting and stopping coadministration.
pairs.source_attribution: Liverpool HIV Drug Interactions: Dolutegravir + Metformin (Potential Interaction); TIVICAY FDA label Table of drug interactions

pairs.description: Rifampicin strongly induces UGT1A1 and CYP3A, which metabolize dolutegravir, markedly lowering dolutegravir concentrations.
pairs.clinical_significance: Once-daily dolutegravir exposure with rifampicin is insufficient and risks virologic failure and integrase resistance, a common issue in HIV/TB co-infection.
pairs.recommendation: The dolutegravir dose is increased to 50 mg twice daily during rifampicin coadministration in integrase-inhibitor-naive adults (for a TLD regimen, by adding a separate dolutegravir 50 mg dose); this adjustment is not suitable for integrase-experienced patients with suspected INSTI resistance.
pairs.source_attribution: TIVICAY (dolutegravir) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 2 Dosage and Section 7 Table of established drug interactions (rifampin)

pairs.description: Zinc and other polyvalent cations chelate dolutegravir in the gastrointestinal tract, reducing its absorption.
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced dolutegravir concentrations may compromise viral suppression; evidence quality for zinc specifically is very low but the effect is expected by class.
pairs.recommendation: Administer dolutegravir-containing regimens 2 hours before or 6 hours after zinc-containing products, or take them together with food.
pairs.source_attribution: Liverpool HIV Drug Interactions: Dolutegravir/lamivudine + Zinc (Potential Interaction); TIVICAY FDA label (polyvalent cations)

pairs.description: Dolutegravir absorption is not meaningfully affected by gastric acid suppression; omeprazole is not listed among drugs requiring dose change with dolutegravir.
pairs.clinical_significance: The dolutegravir label lists omeprazole among drugs without clinically significant interactions.
pairs.recommendation: Can be coadministered without dose adjustment (note: this does not apply to cation-containing antacids, which require dose separation).
pairs.source_attribution: TIVICAY (dolutegravir) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drugs without Clinically Significant Interactions

pairs.description: Prednisone did not meaningfully alter dolutegravir pharmacokinetics in interaction studies.
pairs.clinical_significance: The dolutegravir label lists prednisone among drugs that can be coadministered without dose adjustment.
pairs.recommendation: Can be coadministered without dose adjustment of the dolutegravir component.
pairs.source_attribution: TIVICAY (dolutegravir) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drugs without Clinically Significant Interactions

pairs.description: Trimethoprim inhibits renal cationic secretion of lamivudine; co-trimoxazole increased lamivudine AUC by about 43% and reduced its renal clearance by about 30%.
pairs.clinical_significance: The increase is not considered clinically significant at standard co-trimoxazole doses; the combination is routine when co-trimoxazole prophylaxis is given with antiretroviral therapy. Effects of high (PCP-treatment) doses on lamivudine have not been studied.
pairs.recommendation: No dose adjustment of lamivudine is needed at standard co-trimoxazole doses; renal function is reviewed in patients with renal impairment.
pairs.source_attribution: EPIVIR (lamivudine) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions (trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole); applies to the lamivudine component of TLD

pairs.description: Both are renally eliminated HBV antivirals, but interaction studies showed no change in the steady-state pharmacokinetics of either drug.
pairs.clinical_significance: Entecavir is not a CYP450 substrate, inhibitor or inducer; no pharmacokinetic interaction was observed with tenofovir DF, lamivudine or adefovir.
pairs.recommendation: No pharmacokinetic dose adjustment is required; both drugs are dose-adjusted for creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min and renal function is monitored.
pairs.source_attribution: BARACLUDE (entecavir) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions and Clinical Pharmacology

pairs.description: Sulfamethoxazole inhibits CYP2C9, the main enzyme metabolizing S-warfarin, and may displace warfarin from protein binding.
pairs.clinical_significance: Co-trimoxazole may prolong prothrombin time and raise INR, increasing bleeding risk.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor INR closely during and shortly after co-trimoxazole therapy and adjust warfarin dose as needed; an alternative antibiotic may be considered.
pairs.source_attribution: BACTRIM (sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim) FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions (warfarin)

pairs.description: Trimethoprim inhibits the renal organic cation transporter OCT2 (and MATE), reducing tubular secretion of metformin.
pairs.clinical_significance: Co-trimoxazole potentiates the glucose-lowering effect of metformin; increased metformin exposure is a concern in renal impairment.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose during coadministration and review renal function; adjust antidiabetic therapy as needed.
pairs.source_attribution: BACTRIM (sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim) FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions (oral hypoglycemics eliminated renally via OCT2)

pairs.description: Sulfonamides potentiate the glucose-lowering effect of sulfonylureas; sulfamethoxazole inhibits CYP2C9, a pathway of sulfonylurea metabolism.
pairs.clinical_significance: Potentiation of the blood-glucose-lowering effect, and in some instances hypoglycaemia, may occur, particularly in older adults or with renal impairment.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose closely during and after the co-trimoxazole course and adjust the gliclazide dose as needed.
pairs.source_attribution: Gliclazide MR Canadian product monograph (Drug Interactions: sulfonamides); BACTRIM FDA label (CYP2C9 sulfonylurea potentiation)

pairs.description: Trimethoprim blocks the epithelial sodium channel in the distal nephron (amiloride-like effect), reducing potassium excretion; ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone.
pairs.clinical_significance: Additive potassium retention; hyperkalemia has been reported in elderly patients after concomitant co-trimoxazole and an ACE inhibitor.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium closely, especially in older adults and renal impairment; consider an alternative antibiotic when clinically appropriate.
pairs.source_attribution: BACTRIM (sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim) FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions (angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor) and Hyperkalemia

pairs.description: Trimethoprim's amiloride-like reduction of distal potassium secretion adds to the aldosterone-lowering effect of angiotensin receptor blockers.
pairs.clinical_significance: In a population-based study of older adults on ACE inhibitors or ARBs, co-trimoxazole was associated with about a 7-fold higher risk of hospital admission for hyperkalemia compared with amoxicillin (adjusted OR 6.7).
pairs.recommendation: Consider an alternative antibiotic when clinically appropriate; if co-trimoxazole is used, monitor serum potassium and renal function.
pairs.source_attribution: Antoniou T et al. Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole-Induced Hyperkalemia in Patients Receiving Inhibitors of the Renin-Angiotensin System. Arch Intern Med. 2010

pairs.description: Trimethoprim and spironolactone both reduce renal potassium excretion (ENaC blockade and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism).
pairs.clinical_significance: Concomitant use may result in clinically relevant hyperkalaemia; EU product information for spironolactone was updated to include this interaction. Observational data in older adults show a markedly increased risk of hyperkalaemia admission.
pairs.recommendation: Prefer an alternative antibiotic where feasible; if used together, monitor serum potassium and renal function closely and consider temporary dose reduction of spironolactone.
pairs.source_attribution: EMA CMDh scientific conclusions, altizide/spironolactone PSUSA (2015): interaction with trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole

pairs.description: Mechanism is not established; the interaction is reported with concurrent sulfonamide-trimethoprim and diuretic therapy, primarily thiazides.
pairs.clinical_significance: An increased incidence of thrombocytopenia with purpura has been reported in elderly patients receiving certain diuretics, primarily thiazides, with co-trimoxazole.
pairs.recommendation: In older adults, monitor for bruising, petechiae or bleeding and check platelet count if symptoms occur.
pairs.source_attribution: BACTRIM (sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim) FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions (diuretics)

pairs.description: Rifampicin is a strong CYP3A inducer and markedly reduces praziquantel plasma concentrations.
pairs.clinical_significance: Concomitant use can lead to subtherapeutic praziquantel levels and treatment failure; the label lists it as a contraindication.
pairs.recommendation: Contraindicated. If praziquantel treatment is required, the label advises discontinuing rifampicin 2-4 weeks beforehand; rifampicin can be restarted one day after praziquantel treatment is completed.
pairs.source_attribution: BILTRICIDE (praziquantel) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 4 Contraindications and Section 7 Drug Interactions (strong CYP3A inducers)

pairs.description: Ritonavir inhibits CYP3A-mediated metabolism of praziquantel.
pairs.clinical_significance: Praziquantel plasma concentrations may increase, which may increase dose-related adverse effects (dizziness, headache, abdominal discomfort).
pairs.recommendation: Monitor for praziquantel adverse effects; where feasible, deworming can be timed after the 5-day nirmatrelvir/ritonavir course.
pairs.source_attribution: BILTRICIDE (praziquantel) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions (CYP450 inhibitors including ritonavir)

pairs.description: Systemic corticosteroids and other immunosuppressive agents can interfere with the development of active immunity after rabies vaccination.
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced neutralizing antibody response during post-exposure prophylaxis may leave the patient unprotected against rabies.
pairs.recommendation: Immunosuppressive agents are not given during post-exposure prophylaxis unless essential for another condition; in immunosuppressed patients, serum rabies antibody is tested (e.g., on Day 14) to confirm an adequate response.
pairs.source_attribution: RabAvert (rabies vaccine, PCECV) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 5 Altered Immunocompetence and Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Rabies immunoglobulin provides passive neutralizing antibody but can partially suppress the active antibody response to rabies vaccine if given in excess or at the same site.
pairs.clinical_significance: Standard complementary combination for category III exposures in previously unvaccinated persons; an excessive or repeated RIG dose may impair vaccine immunogenicity.
pairs.recommendation: Give a single RIG dose (HRIG 20 IU/kg) infiltrated into and around the wound(s), with any remainder IM at a site distant from the vaccine; never in the same syringe or anatomical site as the vaccine; do not exceed the recommended dose; RIG is not given to previously vaccinated persons.
pairs.source_attribution: HYPERRAB (rabies immune globulin [human]) FDA label (DailyMed), Section 2 Dosage and Administration and Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Zinc and other multivalent cations form chelation complexes with fluoroquinolones in the gut, reducing ciprofloxacin absorption.
pairs.clinical_significance: Markedly reduced ciprofloxacin bioavailability can result in treatment failure, relevant when zinc is given with antibiotics in pediatric diarrhea.
pairs.recommendation: Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after zinc-containing products.
pairs.source_attribution: Ciprofloxacin tablets FDA label (DailyMed), Section 2 and Section 7 (products containing calcium, iron or zinc)

pairs.description: Cetirizine is minimally metabolized by CYP3A. Full-dose ritonavir (600 mg twice daily) increased cetirizine AUC by 42%, similar to exposures seen in older adults or mild renal impairment.
pairs.clinical_significance: With ritonavir used as a pharmacokinetic booster, a clinically significant interaction is not expected.
pairs.recommendation: Can be coadministered without dose adjustment (nirmatrelvir itself was not studied; assessment is based on cetirizine's minimal metabolism).
pairs.source_attribution: Liverpool HIV Drug Interactions: Ritonavir + Cetirizine (No Interaction Expected)

rules.name: Hyperkalemia triad (co-trimoxazole + RAAS blocker + potassium-sparing diuretic)
rules.description: Trimethoprim blocks distal-nephron sodium channels (amiloride-like), ACE inhibitors/ARBs lower aldosterone, and spironolactone antagonizes the mineralocorticoid receptor; all three reduce renal potassium excretion.
rules.clinical_significance: The co-trimoxazole label warns that even recommended doses may cause hyperkalemia when drugs known to induce hyperkalemia are given concomitantly; combining all three compounds the risk of severe hyperkalemia, especially in older adults and renal impairment.
rules.recommendation: Prefer an alternative antibiotic; if co-trimoxazole is unavoidable, check serum potassium and creatinine before and within a few days of starting, and consider temporarily holding spironolactone.
rules.source_attribution: BACTRIM FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Hyperkalemia and Drug Interactions; EMA CMDh 2015 spironolactone/trimethoprim conclusions; Antoniou et al., Arch Intern Med 2010

rules.name: Co-trimoxazole + RAAS blocker in chronic kidney disease
rules.description: Trimethoprim reduces distal potassium secretion; with an ACE inhibitor or ARB and reduced renal function, potassium elimination is further impaired and co-trimoxazole components accumulate.
rules.clinical_significance: The label states hyperkalemia may occur at recommended doses in patients with renal insufficiency or when drugs known to induce hyperkalemia are given concomitantly; half-lives of both components increase in severe renal impairment.
rules.recommendation: Adjust co-trimoxazole dose for creatinine clearance, monitor serum potassium closely, and consider an alternative antibiotic when clinically appropriate.
rules.source_attribution: BACTRIM FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Hyperkalemia; Dosage in renal impairment

rules.name: Tenofovir DF + NSAID in chronic kidney disease
rules.description: Tenofovir DF is renally eliminated and can cause tubular injury; NSAIDs reduce renal perfusion; pre-existing kidney disease reduces reserve.
rules.clinical_significance: Acute renal failure has been reported after initiation of high-dose or multiple NSAIDs in patients with renal risk factors who were stable on tenofovir DF.
rules.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs with tenofovir DF in chronic kidney disease; use paracetamol for analgesia. Tenofovir DF dosing interval is adjusted for creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min, with monitoring of creatinine, urine glucose/protein and phosphorus.
rules.source_attribution: VIREAD (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5.2 and 7.1
